The source manuscript is the retained 107-page `draft-kott-numina-pair-binding-02-final.pdf`: 808,496 bytes, SHA-256 `3e5db9f5ef29b7adb7ce408488b6c78cdd7121732d92efa638157de7a96f3ce9`. ## Exact manuscript reference

Section **15.11, “Presence, null, integrity and output comparison,” pages 36–37**, is the precise legacy-schema reference. The “Legacy schema missing” paragraph on page 37 states that `CompletedLegacyClosureResult` must not be constructed until all eight field names, schema/version, mandatory check-to-field projection, field meanings and required completed evidence are identified. The exact legacy schema, total projection and preservation proofs remain pending in that edition. Section 15.7 supplies a separate tagged assessment/lifecycle, not an implicit Boolean conversion.

This reference names the intended legacy result without supplying its missing definition. Seven named checks do not identify eight legacy fields. Neither inserting an eighth Boolean nor converting unavailable, incomplete, unrun, running or crashed states to `false` supplies the required source.

## Final-manuscript proof identities

The final manuscript uses and records **Lean 4.24.0** evidence. Section 16.6 records the separate corrected core with 95 theorems/239 audited declarations; section 16.6.4 records the ordered pair-wire packet's 4.24.0 compiler/axiom receipt. Appendix Q and Q.1 preserve their distinct source, receipt and review identities. Those final-manuscript results are not replaced, invalidated or downgraded by the later available Lean 4.22.0 bundle. No compiler is run for this note.

The signed delivery separately includes `NCPS-Lean4-Proofs-2026-10-09.zip`, SHA-256 `62b3607544daeb524fb82ad60c7442eb9281f9cfb1862029fc716cfd5a14954e`, and its recorded 4.22.0/131-theorem readback. That bundle's `NCPS.Advanced.VerificationReport` has seven tagged findings, and its `ClosureReport` has seven tagged stages. They are different types from the unresolved eight-Boolean legacy result.

The separately signed [decoded-attribution source](../release-evidence/decoded-attribution-closure-2026-10-11/NCPSAttributionClosure.lean), SHA-256 `92c271842746c45b321ae9dc09d9040a1795662ac9287dd57322a4d526e42cee`, introduces an eight-*finding* model explicitly distinct from the legacy Boolean schema. Its twelve bounded theorems do not recover that historical definition. Do not add theorem counts from distinct packets as a whole-protocol proof count.

## Definition-source status

A bounded read of the canonical `config`, `src`, `api`, `public`, `scripts` and `runtime` roots did not identify a `ClosureResult` or `CompletedLegacyClosureResult` definition. The retained public proof packet and recorded dependency readbacks likewise do not identify the exact legacy field schema/projection. This is a reference-discovery limit, not evidence that the author's original source never existed or was lost.

The existing original engineering archive locator is `libfile_c2887d73285c819197c5674bc2004de3`, with recorded SHA-256 `08a2b5c40fed00559332ed9da81a6006b0725c44769b1162d4b38ca11a2a4d80`. It is a retrieval lead, not a verified legacy-schema definition. `ParserRefinement.lean` and `PairExtraction.lean` are distinct cited imports. No source aliases, field names or projections are inferred from those filenames. Private source content is not republished here.

The current operational control journal's schema-1 event records and any historical Nano N50 journal are separate subjects. Their schemas cannot be relabeled as NCPS `ClosureResult` without an explicit matching definition and projection source.

Next verifiable step: recover the author's original versioned legacy schema and check-to-field projection reference, record their exact source hashes and governing edition, and link them to section 15.11 in a separately identified note. Until then, the exact cross-reference is restored here; the schema-definition and conformance claims remain unestablished.
